statement: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is five times as large as each of its exterior angles. How many sides does the polygon have?

choices.misconception: I found the exterior angle of 30 degrees but divided 180 by it instead of 360.
I took the exterior angle to be 180 divided by 5, which is 36 degrees, and then divided 360 by 36.
I found 360 divided by 30 is 12 and then added 2, mixing it up with the n - 2 in the angle sum formula.
I stopped once I had the exterior angle and gave its size, 30, as the number of sides.

hints: An interior angle and its exterior angle sit together on a straight line.

Split the straight angle at each vertex into six equal shares: one for the exterior angle and five for the interior one. Then use the fact that the exterior angles of any polygon add up to a full turn.
The exterior angle is 180 / 6 = 30 degrees, and all the exterior angles together make 360 degrees.

solutions.reliable: At each vertex the interior and exterior angles add up to 180 degrees. If the exterior angle is x, then x + 5x = 180, so x = 30 degrees. The exterior angles of a convex polygon always add up to 360 degrees, so there are 360 / 30 = 12 of them, and the polygon has 12 sides. Check: a regular 12-gon has angle sum 10 x 180 = 1800 degrees, so each interior angle is 150 degrees, which is five times 30. The transferable idea: for regular polygons, work with the exterior angle, because the exterior angles always total 360 degrees.

whyOnTest: Regular polygon questions test whether you reach for the exterior angle, whose total is always 360 degrees, instead of grinding the interior angle formula.
